stages.name: Emerging and developing economies
stages.title: Emerging and developing economies
stages.sub: Why infrastructure projects can go wrong, and what the World Bank does about the savings gap.

steps.q: A government borrows heavily from abroad to build a new highway. Ten years later, does that money still belong to the government?
steps.right: No, it has to be paid back with interest
steps.wrong: Yes, once spent it is no longer owed
steps.hint: Where did the money for the highway actually come from?
steps.pre: Building big infrastructure is often funded by borrowing, creating a

steps.q: A large share of the government's yearly budget now goes on repaying that highway loan. What happens to spending on things like hospitals and schools?
steps.wrong: It is unaffected, since the loan is separate
steps.hint: The budget is limited. If more goes to one thing, what happens to the rest?
steps.pre: Money spent repaying loans cannot also be spent elsewhere, so there is an

steps.q: The highway also takes five years to build, runs over budget, and mainly benefits the capital city rather than rural areas. Does infrastructure development always deliver smooth, fair benefits to the whole country?
steps.right: No, it can be slow, costly and unevenly spread
steps.wrong: Yes, it always benefits everyone equally and on time
steps.hint: Think about delays, cost overruns and who actually uses the new highway.

steps.q: A country wants to invest in new infrastructure but its citizens simply do not save or earn enough to fund it domestically. Where else could the extra funds come from?
steps.right: Loans or grants from an international institution
steps.wrong: The gap will close by itself over time
steps.hint: If domestic saving cannot cover it, who else lends money to countries?
steps.pre: An international institution can step in to help with

steps.q: This institution lends money to developing countries for projects like roads, dams and schools, often attaching conditions on how the money is used. What is this institution's role called?
steps.right: Providing loans and policy conditions to support development
steps.wrong: Printing extra currency for the country to spend freely
steps.hint: Think about what kind of organisation lends specifically for development projects, not just any bank.
